title: Tenant banding and soft-bursting for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Patel
description: PRD for a tenant-banding approach and an associated soft-burst mechanism for Dedicated capacity. Goal is to provide predictable baseline throughput for committed tenants while enabling short-lived extra capacity (soft-burst) that is safe, auditable, and reversible without violating isolation SLAs. This feature targets mid-to-large customers on Dedicated who need predictable latency and throughput but occasionally experience traffic spikes that should not trigger full preemption or expensive overprovisioning.
background: Current Dedicated model exposes reserved pools per-tenant and global autoscaling rules. Customers ask for: 1) better predictability under noisy neighbors, 2) controlled, short-lived burst above baseline without immediate eviction of other tenants, and 3) an administrative surface to observe and recover burst usage. Existing PRDs focus on reservation sizing and preemptive eviction; this PRD explores banding tenants into soft-priority tiers and funding transient burst from a safety-credit pool.
goals: Guarantee baseline throughput and tail latency for tenants with reserved allocations
Allow short-lived soft-bursting up to a configurable multiplier with graceful decay
Provide controls to define tenant bands (e.g., Gold/Silver/Bronze) with distinct burst behavior
Expose observability and chargeback for burst consumption in Console
Ensure burst mechanism respects isolation SLAs and enables automatic rollback/preemption when safety thresholds are hit
non_goals: Replace existing long-term reservation contracts or billing models
Automate pricing changes for burst usage (billing handled by billing team separately)
Support unbounded burst or multi-hour overcommit without operator approval
personas: Platform engineer at a SaaS company who needs predictable latency for customer-facing endpoints
Solutions engineer onboarding an enterprise customer that expects controlled burst behavior
Ops engineer at Redwood responsible for managing Dedicated clusters and capacity safety
requirements: R1: Tenant banding API - Admins can assign tenants to a band with default burst multiplier and priority weight
R2: Soft-burst pool - A configurable safety-credit pool per-dedicated-cluster that funds transient burst requests
R3: Burst admission control - Runtime accepts burst requests up to band multiplier if pool credits available, else routes to fallback model/queue
R4: Graceful decay - Active bursts should decay linearly or exponentially to baseline over a configurable window (default 60s)
R5: Isolation guardrails - When cluster-level safety thresholds (CPU/GPU utilization, latency SLO) are exceeded, automatically throttle or evict soft-bursting tenants in reverse priority
R6: Console UX - New "Burst" tab in Dedicated tenant page showing current band, burst consumption, credit balance, and recent evictions
R7: Telemetry - Emit burst_approved, burst_rejected, burst_evicted events and per-tenant burst_duration, burst_tokens_consumed metrics
R8: Audit logs - All burst approvals/evictions must be logged to existing audit stream with tenant, band, request id, and decision reason
R9: Admin controls - Operators can top-up or drain cluster safety pool and put clusters into "burst-disabled" maintenance mode
R10: Compatibility - Fall back to existing preemption behavior when soft-burst module is disabled
api_changes: POST /admin/tenant/{id}/band - set band and default multiplier
GET /admin/cluster/{id}/burst-pool - view pool status and consumption
Headers: X-Requested-Burst:true on client requests to mark intent (optional, used for invoicing/telemetry)
console_changes: Dedicated tenant page: new 'Burst' tab showing band, multiplier, recent burst windows
Cluster page: safety pool gauge, top-up button, recent burst events table
Settings: band templates and default multipliers UI for account admins
telemetry: Trace: include burst decision span in request traces to correlate latency changes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary: Enable soft-burst on 2 internal clusters with synthetic workload and real telemetry (2 weeks)
Phase 1 - Opt-in beta: Offer to 3 enterprise customers under feature flag for controlled beta (4 weeks)
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: Enable for 25% of Dedicated clusters with conservative defaults and monitoring (4 weeks)
Phase 3 - GA: Full rollout with admin defaults and documentation (target release dedicated-2026.04)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Tenants assigned to Gold band receive baseline throughput unchanged and can burst up to 2x baseline when pool credits available
AC2: Soft-burst decay ensures no sustained >1.2x baseline beyond 180s for more than 95% of bursts in production canary
AC3: When cluster safety pool drops below threshold (10%), new burst requests are rejected and logged with 'pool_depleted' reason
AC4: Console surfaces burst consumption and audit logs for any cluster where feature is enabled
AC5: Telemetry events for burst decisions are visible in observability dashboards and linked to request traces
AC6: Under simulated noisy-neighbor test, tenants outside burst are not regressed beyond 5th-pct tail increase of 10ms compared to baseline
AC7: Admins can disable burst globally for a cluster and the runtime immediately stops approving new bursts within 30s
success_metrics: SM1: Reduction in customer-reported outage/eviction incidents during transient spikes by 40% for participants
SM2: <5% increase in operational evictions attributable to bursts after 8 weeks of ramp
SM3: Average burst acceptance rate > 70% for Gold band tenants in beta
SM4: Observability dashboards show burst-related metrics within 5 minutes of event
dependencies_details: ENG: runtime admission controller changes to check band + pool credits (ENG-91234)
ENG: telemetry pipeline to accept new burst events (ENG-91827)
Design: Console UX mockups and accessibility review (DES-3247)
Billing: alignment on whether X-Requested-Burst gets charged differently (PM-712459)
open_questions: Q1: What is default multiplier per band (Gold=2x, Silver=1.5x, Bronze=1.25x)? Decision needed from pricing before GA
Q2: Should burst credits be per-cluster only or allocatable per-tenant ledger? Tradeoffs: simplicity vs fairness
Q3: Which metrics constitute cluster 'safety thresholds' (GPU SM utilization, 99th latency, queue length)?
Q4: Billing: do we bill burst consumption as overage or include as part of committed units?
Q5: What UI permissions are required for top-up/drain actions in Console?
notes: Security: KMS keys required only for audit export; security review scheduled with SSO and audit team
